diagrams.title: Sell a Measured Scope, Then Prove Delivery
diagrams.subtitle: Five operating stages for recurring commercial and medical janitorial contracts.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Recognized operator revenue is earned cleaning contract revenue. Customer building value, tenant sales, and proposed contract value are excluded. Higher revenue requires additional paid productive crew hours, higher realized pricing, or both.
diagrams.caption: The workflow connects the bid estimate to actual paid hours, documented service quality, invoicing, and renewal pricing.

stages.label: Qualify the route
stages.value: Confirm buyer, location, frequency, and payment terms
stages.detail: Record the facility manager, purchasing authority, building address, service windows, invoice requirements, and travel time from existing stops. Flag customer concentration before adding a large account.

stages.label: Measure the scope
stages.value: Inventory cleanable area and task-level service frequencies
stages.detail: Walk the site with the buyer; count restrooms, fixtures, floor types, touchpoints, waste stations, and restricted rooms. Distinguish usable cleanable area from leased area and separate periodic floor work from nightly service.

stages.label: Price paid capacity
stages.value: Convert observed production into fully loaded labor costs
stages.detail: Estimate area tasks as square feet divided by task-specific ISSA production-rate references. Add fixture tasks, setup, paid travel, inspections, breaks where required, and rework. Validate with a timed pilot and include payroll burden, overtime, supplies, overhead, and target profit.

stages.label: Mobilize and inspect
stages.value: Assign qualified labor and capture completed-task evidence
stages.detail: Use Swept or a comparable scheduling and inspection system to assign employee work, record exceptions, and track corrective actions. Independently operated subcontractors deliver contracted outcomes under their own lawful methods.

stages.label: Bill and renew
stages.value: Reconcile accepted services, collection timing, and account margin
stages.detail: Issue QuickBooks invoices against contracted service periods and approved extras. Compare actual hours with the bid weekly; correct scope creep, repeated callbacks, and slow payment before the next renewal.

diagrams.title: One Prospect Cohort, Five Measurable Conversions
diagrams.subtitle: Illustrative account counts; every downstream account belongs to the original cohort.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Follow 200 unique local accounts for up to 120 days, consistent with a one-to-four-month first-deal planning range. Counts are illustrative, not market benchmarks or annual revenue projections. Referred or newly discovered accounts enter separate cohorts.
diagrams.caption: The cohort narrows from 200 researched accounts to five activated contracts: 2.5% overall conversion without mixing leads and locations.

stages.label: Researched accounts
stages.value: 200 unique accounts matching the service territory
stages.detail: Deduplicate legal buyers and document facility type, route distance, estimated cleaning frequency, and a reachable purchasing contact before counting an account.

stages.label: Qualified conversations
stages.value: 80 accounts with confirmed need and purchasing access
stages.detail: Forty percent of the original accounts confirm a relevant service need, a buyer contact, and a plausible buying window. Email opens and unanswered calls do not qualify.

stages.label: Completed walkthroughs
stages.value: 40 accounts with measured sites and service requirements
stages.detail: Fifty percent of qualified conversations produce a completed site inspection with task inventory, access conditions, existing service problems, and invoice requirements.

stages.label: Delivered proposals
stages.value: 20 accounts receive costed and capacity-checked proposals
stages.detail: Fifty percent of walkthrough accounts receive priced scopes after labor-hour costing and route review. Decline work that cannot cover required wages and delivery costs.

stages.label: Activated contracts
stages.value: Five accounts sign and begin accepted service
stages.detail: Twenty-five percent of proposed accounts sign and start service within the observation window. Track deposits, earned revenue, invoiced receivables, and cash collections separately.

diagrams.title: $725,000 Contract Revenue to $87,000 Owner Net
diagrams.subtitle: Six bars reconcile the Base-Case annual operating result to a 12.0% net margin.
diagrams.assumptions_note: USD per year. The first and last bars are absolute totals; the four middle bars are negative movements. Intermediate balances are $290,000, $246,500, $166,750, and $87,000. Cost categories are an illustrative allocation, not additional canonical scorecard inputs. Owner net is the operating residual before owner-specific income taxes.
diagrams.caption: $725,000 minus $435,000 minus $43,500 minus $79,750 minus $79,750 equals $87,000. Costs total $638,000, or 88.0% of revenue; owner net equals 12.0%. The stated $3,000–$14,000 monthly opex range cannot serve as an all-in cost ceiling for this scenario; its coverage must be reconciled before bidding.

stages.label: Earned contract revenue
stages.value: $725,000 annual cleaning service revenue; opening total
stages.detail: Use the canonical Base-Case gross revenue for completed cleaning services. Exclude sales taxes collected for remittance and customer business turnover.

stages.label: Direct service labor
stages.value: Subtract $435,000 for paid delivery labor and burden
stages.detail: Allocate 60.0% of revenue to field employee wages, employer payroll charges, field workers' compensation, paid travel, overtime, callbacks, and legitimate subcontract service invoices. Remaining balance: $290,000.

stages.label: Supplies and equipment
stages.value: Subtract $43,500 for chemicals, consumables, and equipment
stages.detail: Allocate 6.0% of revenue to cleaning chemicals, liners, microfiber replacement, equipment rental or depreciation, and repairs. Keep equipment purchase cash flows separate from annual expense recognition. Remaining balance: $246,500.

stages.label: Supervision and operations
stages.value: Subtract $79,750 for oversight and shared operating costs
stages.detail: Allocate 11.0% of revenue to supervisor compensation and burden, management work, vehicles, storage, general liability, and inspection systems. Assign each payroll hour once; exclude field labor already charged above. Remaining balance: $166,750.

stages.label: Selling and administration
stages.value: Subtract $79,750 for acquisition, billing, and administration
stages.detail: Allocate 11.0% of revenue to estimating, account sales, administrative compensation and burden, accounting, payment fees, bad-debt expense, and other operating expenses. Include compensation for owner work where applicable before calculating residual profit. Remaining balance: $87,000.

stages.label: Annual owner net
stages.value: $87,000 residual owner profit; closing total at 12.0%
stages.detail: Render this bar from zero, not as another positive movement. Preserve the other canonical scenarios: $250,000 at 8.0% yields $20,000; $1,200,000 at 16.0% yields $192,000.

diagrams.title: Compare Contribution per Paid Service Hour
diagrams.subtitle: Five illustrative sub-niche bids after direct delivery costs, before shared overhead.
diagrams.assumptions_note: All values are USD contribution per paid service hour, not net margin percentages or published market rates. Revenue equivalent equals contract revenue divided by all attributable paid service hours. Direct cost includes loaded field labor, routine consumables, and service-specific equipment. Shared supervision, sales, administration, and owner net remain outside these bars.
diagrams.caption: Rank measured account economics rather than building labels. Extra dwell time, access delays, overtime, and rework can erase a nominal medical or industrial price premium.

stages.label: Outpatient medical offices
stages.value: $14 contribution from $52 revenue less $38 direct cost
stages.detail: Model label contact times, isolation-area restrictions, PPE, and exposure-related training in paid hours. Do not price regulated waste handling into an ordinary janitorial scope without the required operating capability.

stages.label: Light industrial offices
stages.value: $12 contribution from $48 revenue less $36 direct cost
stages.detail: Limit the modeled scope to offices and agreed common areas. Separately quote production-floor work, machinery proximity, unusual soils, and site-specific safety training.

stages.label: Professional office suites
stages.value: $11 contribution from $44 revenue less $33 direct cost
stages.detail: Cluster nearby suites to reduce paid travel. Measure desk density, restroom fixtures, alarm procedures, elevator delays, and tenant-requested extras rather than bidding from square footage alone.

stages.label: Multitenant common areas
stages.value: $11 contribution from $46 revenue less $35 direct cost
stages.detail: Specify lobby appearance standards, restroom replenishment, public access windows, and weekend attendance. Separate tenant-private cleaning from property-manager common-area obligations to prevent unpaid scope expansion.

stages.label: Private education facilities
stages.value: $8 contribution from $40 revenue less $32 direct cost
stages.detail: Price restroom intensity, event resets, safeguarding-related access procedures, and academic calendar changes. Quote summer floor restoration separately and confirm whether monthly billing continues through closures.

diagrams.title: Four Checks Before Assigning a Crew
diagrams.subtitle: Each failed check routes to a specific correction before the affected work starts.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Read nodes in order. Each numeric value is a sequence index, not a risk score or probability. Apply federal requirements alongside applicable state and local rules. Insurance limits depend on jurisdiction, policy terms, and the buyer's contract.
diagrams.caption: A signed cleaning agreement does not cure underpaid labor, misclassification, unsafe chemical use, or uninsured scope.

stages.label: Wages and paid time
stages.value: Pass to classification; otherwise recost and correct payroll
stages.detail: Apply 29 U.S.C. 206 and 207 to covered workers, including overtime for covered nonexempt employees. Keep required records under 29 CFR Part 516 and evaluate compensable time under 29 CFR Part 785. Capture intersite travel and setup; apply higher applicable state or local wage requirements.

stages.label: Actual worker relationship
stages.value: Pass to chemical review; otherwise redesign or employ
stages.detail: Evaluate actual control and economic facts under applicable FLSA, tax, and state tests, including 26 U.S.C. 3121(d)(2) and California Labor Code section 2775 where relevant. A 1099 form, LLC, or insurance certificate alone does not establish independent status.

stages.label: Chemical and exposure controls
stages.value: Pass to contract review; otherwise train and correct methods
stages.detail: Implement applicable 29 CFR 1910.1200 labeling, safety data sheets, written program, and training requirements. Follow disinfectant labeling under 7 U.S.C. 136j. Where occupational exposure exists, implement 29 CFR 1910.1030 controls; do not assign untrained workers to sharps or blood cleanup.

stages.label: Insured and bounded scope
stages.value: Start covered work only after resolving identified coverage gaps
stages.detail: Confirm required workers' compensation and buyer-specified liability coverage with the broker. Review exclusions, endorsements, key loss, property damage, and medical-site activities. Attach service frequencies, inspection standards, change-order pricing, payment terms, and termination rights to the signed agreement.

diagrams.title: Four Core Seats, Two Explicit Expansion Seats
diagrams.subtitle: Conservative and Base: 1 FT + 3 C (4 people). Scaled: 2 FT + 4 C (6 people).
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values indicate active Conservative and Base core seats: four ones and two zeros. The core comprises 1 FT + 3 C; activate the two zero-valued seats, 1 FT + 1 C, only in the Scaled scenario for 2 FT + 4 C. FT denotes full-time employee seats; C denotes one-person independent service-provider seats, subject to applicable classification tests. Headcount is not a full-time-equivalent measure. External vendor/trade sub-crews are charged to direct subcontractor/COGS pass-through, not internal pod headcount; their delivery capacity and costs must still be measured and funded.
diagrams.caption: Conservative: $250,000 revenue and $20,000 owner net with four people (1 FT + 3 C). Base: $725,000 revenue and $87,000 owner net with four people (1 FT + 3 C). Scaled: $1,200,000 revenue and $192,000 owner net with six people (2 FT + 4 C). These are separate operating scenarios, not proof that two added seats alone produce the revenue increase. Validate paid hours, external delivery capacity, utilization, pricing, and route capacity before accepting added work.

stages.label: FT 1: pod supervisor and account operations
stages.value: One active employee owning delivery quality, estimates, and billing
stages.detail: Own site mobilization, inspection review, supply readiness, proposal costing, invoice follow-up, and renewals. Coordinate contracted provider outcomes without imposing employee-style methods on independent businesses. Maintain weekly bid-hours versus actual-hours reporting and verify external delivery coverage. If the owner fills this seat, include their work compensation before residual owner net.

stages.label: C 1: floor-care provider
stages.value: One active independent provider delivering bounded floor projects
stages.detail: Contract for defined floor-care outcomes with an independently operated provider using appropriate equipment and methods. Verify insurance, competence, scheduling interfaces, and classification under the actual working arrangement.

stages.label: C 2: carpet-care provider
stages.value: One active independent provider delivering scheduled extraction projects
stages.detail: Purchase scoped carpet extraction outcomes with documented drying requirements, access windows, and property protection. Do not disguise an employee cleaner's regular controlled shift as a specialist subcontract.

stages.label: C 3: interior-glass provider
stages.value: One active independent provider delivering scoped glass services
stages.detail: Define reachable interior-glass surfaces, frequency, and acceptance evidence. Exclude elevated-access work unless the provider has suitable equipment, training, insurance, and an expressly priced scope.

stages.label: FT 2: scaled working lead
stages.value: Zero core seats; activate one employee for Scaled capacity
stages.detail: Add this second full-time employee only against measured recurring paid-hour demand and adequate collection funding. Perform cleaning and support inspection and route coverage. Record supervisory and field time separately; recalculate overtime exposure and supervisor capacity before expanding.

stages.label: C 4: scaled project-cleaning provider
stages.value: Zero core seats; activate one independent provider for Scaled demand
stages.detail: Add a fourth genuine one-person provider for independently priced deep-cleaning projects with bounded deliverables, not employee-style fill-in shifts. External vendor/trade sub-crews remain direct subcontractor/COGS pass-through rather than additional internal pod seats. Verify their capacity, insurance, and lawful working arrangements.

diagrams.title: Allocate a $30,000 Reference Launch Budget
diagrams.subtitle: Four buckets reconcile $10,000 lean, $30,000 reference, and $50,000 expanded plans.
diagrams.assumptions_note: All amounts are USD. Numeric values encode only the $30,000 central/reference startup stack within the canonical $10,000–$50,000 startup capital range. The value text supplies comparable $10,000 lean and $50,000 expanded stacks in the same four-bucket order. These are startup cash allocations, not annual expenses or revenue scenarios. Do not stack all three budgets together.
diagrams.caption: Lean: $3,000 + $1,500 + $500 + $5,000 = $10,000. Reference: $8,000 + $3,500 + $1,500 + $17,000 = $30,000. Expanded: $13,000 + $6,000 + $3,000 + $28,000 = $50,000. A lean launch uses existing transport and staged commitments. None of these budgets guarantees runway for the four-person core pod (1 FT + 3 C), external delivery crews, or expansion to six people (2 FT + 4 C); model mobilization and collections.

stages.label: Equipment and initial supplies
stages.value: Lean $3,000; reference $8,000; expanded $13,000 equipment cash
stages.detail: Allocate $3,000 lean, $8,000 reference, or $13,000 expanded to commercial vacuums, carts, microfiber systems, PPE, dispensers, and initial chemicals. Rent infrequent specialty machines until contracted utilization supports ownership. Avoid duplicating client-provided or independent provider-owned equipment in the budget.

stages.label: Setup and coverage deposits
stages.value: Lean $1,500; reference $3,500; expanded $6,000 setup cash
stages.detail: Allocate $1,500 lean, $3,500 reference, or $6,000 expanded to registration, required local licensing, insurance deposits, contract preparation, and initial safety training. Replace estimates with jurisdiction-specific fees and written broker quotations before committing funds.

stages.label: Acquisition and operating systems
stages.value: Lean $500; reference $1,500; expanded $3,000 acquisition cash
stages.detail: Allocate $500 lean, $1,500 reference, or $3,000 expanded to a focused website, local prospect research, walkthrough travel, estimating setup, and appropriately staged Swept and QuickBooks configuration. Limit subscription seats and advertising commitments until the first route converts.

stages.label: Payroll and collection buffer
stages.value: Lean $5,000; reference $17,000; expanded $28,000 liquidity
stages.detail: Hold $5,000 lean, $17,000 reference, or $28,000 expanded as unspent cash for wages, payroll charges, subcontract invoices, and collection delays. At Base-Case direct service labor of $435,000 yearly, the $17,000 reference buffer covers about two weeks of that cost alone. External vendor/trade sub-crews are direct subcontractor/COGS pass-through, not internal pod headcount. Stage mobilization and model all other cash outflows separately.

diagrams.title: Thirty Days to a Measured, Bid-Ready Operation
diagrams.subtitle: Four weekly milestones establish demand evidence, delivery economics, and launch readiness.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values are milestone end days: 7, 14, 21, and 30. A first signed deal may take one to four months. The sprint builds a qualified pipeline and costed delivery system; service starts only when an actual customer contract and ready capacity support them.
diagrams.caption: Use evidence at each milestone: named accounts, measured walkthroughs, reconciled bids, and a funded mobilization plan. Scheduling, inspection logs, and billing reduce administration but do not replace paid cleaning hours.

stages.label: Days 1-7
stages.value: Choose the territory and establish costed operating boundaries
stages.detail: Select one dense office or outpatient cluster, research 40 named buyer accounts, obtain insurance quotations, and document applicable wage and classification rules. Build the first loaded hourly-cost worksheet and choose the startup cash envelope.

stages.label: Days 8-14
stages.value: Conduct walkthroughs and test task-level production assumptions
stages.detail: Target three completed walkthroughs where buyers agree to participate. Record cleanable area, fixtures, access, and frequencies; perform an authorized timed pilot. Use ISSA references only as initial estimates and retain observed paid-hour evidence.

stages.label: Days 15-21
stages.value: Issue reconciled proposals and verify deliverable labor capacity
stages.detail: Target two complete proposals supported by measured scopes. Test overtime, route travel, supplies, payment delays, and customer concentration. Confirm employee availability and separately scoped provider capability without committing unfunded payroll.

stages.label: Days 22-30
stages.value: Prepare mobilization and continue documented buyer follow-up
stages.detail: Configure scheduling, inspection forms, invoice templates, chemical records, and site-access controls. If a contract is signed, confirm coverage and training before service. Otherwise continue the same prospect cohort into months two through four without recording proposed sales as revenue.
